chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about eating garlic, so he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade it only because of its smell, so he said: 'The one who eats this bad vegetable should not approach our mosques.' As for the one who eats it and does not come to the mosque, there is no problem.'

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on eating garlic before entering a mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the prohibition against garlic is rooted in the etiquette of removing harm (raf' al-adha) rather than inherent impurity, a distinction central to Shia fiqh. It highlights the Prophet's practical wisdom in linking the restriction to mosque attendance, thereby allowing consumption for those who do not disturb the congregation. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on contextual application of prophetic traditions based on social interaction.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about eating the garlic, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade from it due to its smell, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who eats this bad vegetable, so he should not go near our Masjids. So as for the one who eats it and does not come to the Masjid, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about garlic. He (the Imam) said, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, prohibited it only because of its smell, saying, “Whoever eats this filthy vegetable must not come near our Masjid, however, for those who eat it and do not come to the Masjid it is not unlawful.’””
